ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the right-side figure ②, the labels of the seawater isotherms are 22℃ at the top, 20℃ in the middle, and 18℃ at the bottom, and the dashed-line ocean current is located toward the right side of the figure. Then reason: Seawater temperature generally decreases from low latitudes toward high latitudes. In figure ②, the temperature is higher at the top and lower at the bottom, indicating that the low-latitude direction closer to the equator is at the top of the figure, that is, toward the north; the equator is on the north side, so the location should be in the Southern Hemisphere. raw_record.question_text:
Read the following figure and complete:

<image1>

In the two seawater isotherm maps in the figure, the dashed lines indicate ocean currents. Fill in the blank to complete the selected statement: ② is located in ____.

method.method_draft: First describe the right panel: its isotherms are arranged with 22℃ above, 20℃ in the middle, and 18℃ below. Then apply the rule that ocean temperature becomes lower from low latitude to high latitude. Since the warmer side is toward the top/north and the colder side is toward the bottom/south, the direction toward the equator is northward; this pattern corresponds to a location in the Southern Hemisphere. Fill the blank with “南半球”.
method.CoT_raw: 先描述图像：右侧②图中，海水等温线的标注为上方22℃、中间20℃、下方18℃，虚线洋流位于图中偏右位置。再推理：海水温度一般从低纬度向高纬度降低。②图上方温度较高、下方温度较低，说明靠近赤道的低纬方向在图的上方，即向北；赤道在北侧，地点应位于南半球。因此②位于南半球。
method.CoT_answer_check_final: 先描述图像：右侧②图中，海水等温线的标注为上方22℃、中间20℃、下方18℃，虚线洋流位于图中偏右位置。再推理：海水温度一般从低纬度向高纬度降低。②图上方温度较高、下方温度较低，说明靠近赤道的低纬方向在图的上方，即向北；赤道在北侧，地点应位于南半球。因此②位于南半球。
method.CoT_qualify_0: 该推理轨迹符合要求：先描述右侧②图的等温线数值分布和虚线位置，再依据海水温度从低纬向高纬降低进行判断，最终得到②位于南半球，与标准答案一致。图像依据充分，方法草稿遵循良好。
method.CoT_final: 先描述图像：右侧②图中，海水等温线的标注为上方22℃、中间20℃、下方18℃，虚线洋流位于图中偏右位置。再推理：海水温度一般从低纬度向高纬度降低。②图上方温度较高、下方温度较低，说明靠近赤道的低纬方向在图的上方，即向北；赤道在北侧，地点应位于南半球。因此②位于南半球。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Uses only the background meridional temperature gradient shown by the isotherm labels in the right-hand panel; it does not need to classify the current as warm/cold first. This is the most direct route to the hemisphere.
planner_metadata.image_role: Inspect the right-hand sea-temperature diagram labeled ②. Read the isotherm values: the upper isotherm is 22℃, the middle is 20℃, and the lower is 18℃, so temperature is higher toward the top of the panel and lower toward the bottom.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the text to identify that the target is diagram ② and that the task asks for its hemispheric location, not for the current type.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: On a normally oriented map, north is up. Sea surface temperature generally decreases from the equator toward the poles. If temperature increases upward, the equatorward side is upward/north, which means the area lies south of the equator, i.e. in the Southern Hemisphere.

method.method_draft: First compare the two panels’ temperature order. Diagram ① has colder water above and warmer water below, the typical Northern Hemisphere pattern when north is upward. Diagram ② has the opposite order: warmer water above and colder water below. Therefore, in ② the equatorward, warmer direction is upward/north, which means the mapped sea area is in the Southern Hemisphere. Fill the blank as “南半球”.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中有两幅海水等温线图，左图标为①，右图标为②，虚线表示洋流。①中等温线数值从上到下依次为18℃、20℃、22℃，即上方较冷、下方较暖。②中等温线数值从上到下依次为22℃、20℃、18℃，即上方较暖、下方较冷。推理：海水温度通常由低纬向高纬递减，越接近赤道越暖。②表现为图中上方温度较高、下方温度较低，说明上方为低纬、向赤道方向；若按地图通常上北下南，则该海区位于赤道以南，即南半球。因此②位于南半球。

The core geographic law is still the latitude-temperature relationship, so the route is related but not merely a wording change.
planner_metadata.image_role: Inspect both diagrams. In diagram ① the isotherm values go from 18℃ at the top to 22℃ at the bottom, while in diagram ② they are reversed, with 22℃ at the top and 18℃ at the bottom. Note that ② is the right-hand panel marked with the circled number near the lower right.

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: For sea-surface isotherm maps, the hemisphere can be judged from whether temperature increases southward or northward: in the Northern Hemisphere, moving southward toward the equator usually becomes warmer; in the Southern Hemisphere, moving northward toward the equator usually becomes warmer.
